subtallies.name: Who authors the tree, and does a node carry a schema?
cells: Salesforce B2C (classification category + ancestors — the one merchant-authored precedent, and the one that inherits)
merchant-authored, no schema on the tree

framing: The split is not about depth — it is about who authors. No vendor publishes a depth rule or an “earns a node” criterion; the closest is Amazon's and Google's “most specific”, both guidance. The schema-carrying set (7) is the six central authors + Salesforce, which is also the only one that inherits down the tree — the closest analogue to our situation, not an outlier. The spread 107 : 764 : 5,595 : 14,606 tracks what the tree is FOR, not how detailed groceries are.

rows.h: per product type, materialised; not creatable by sellers
rows.shape: FoodAndBeverages.xsd roots at FoodAndBeverages with ProductType an xsd:choice of 107 element refs; the JSON registry floor is 1,640 distinct …/ProductType/<name>; “no global count is well defined.” Schema per product type, one JSON Schema per call. Stated: product types are not creatable — 12 patterns over 877 doc files → 0 hits; additions are announced via PRODUCT_TYPE_DEFINITIONS_CHANGE.NewProductTypes; a seller may only “submit a request to update it using the Category update tool.” Inference: 107 is small because Amazon, not the seller, pays for every one. The join is mutable in Amazon's hands: 15,299 of 26,135 flavour release-note rows are “attribute deleted and no longer associated with the product type.”

14,606 categories, 26 verticals, max level 7; food branch 764 nodes, max level 6. Schema per node — median 6 attributes, 1.04 % carry none. Stated purpose, not depth rule (repo README): “Our open-source, standardized product taxonomy establishes a universal language for product classification … Spanning 25+ essential verticals.” Nothing about what earns a node (the repo's docs/ not in the sparse checkout). Live 2026-09-21: Coffee 11 attributes, Pasta & Noodles 6, Chocolate 6, Snack Foods 5.

rows.h: deep and free because nobody authors a schema per node
rows.shape: 5,595 nodes, 21 roots, depth 7; “every line is id - path” — no schema. Stated: “All products are automatically assigned a product category from Google's continuously evolving product taxonomy.” Inference: depth is cheap for Google because the taxonomy is an ad-targeting classification the platform fills in for you.

Sandbox tree 17,105 nodes, 15,111 leaves (three operations agree); production tree not fetched. Schema per leaf — “Each category has a different set of aspects.” Gap pass 2026-09-21: Food & Beverages subtree has 122 leaves; grocery leaves carry 24–27 aspects each (6–14 variation-enabled).

6,967 product types in one flat map; 383,947 attribute slots, 6,576 distinct names; $ref = 0 across 451,013,258 B. Schema materialised in full per product type; the workbook taxonomy (24 / 77 / 461) is not in the feed.
A tree with has_children; schema per leaf — “Each product category has different attribute data.” Size not published (“there is nothing to count”).

rows.h: Era A 3-level; Era B 3-level (v1) or 7-level (v2, US)
rows.shape: Era A: a 3-level tree (category_version v1), axes per category via get_variant?cat_id=. Era B: “For US shops, pass v2, which represents the 7-level category tree. For other regions, v1 represents the 3-level category tree and is the default.” Schema per leaf via GET /product/202309/categories/{id}/attributes.
Seller-authored nodes carrying is_top_level, parent_category, path_to_root, root_category; no per-category attribute set exists — the only gate is allowed_object_types.

rows.h: the one merchant-authored per-node schema — and it inherits
rows.shape: Merchant-authored catalogs; the classification category's attribute groups plus “any parent categories” — the union of global groups + the classification category's groups + its ancestors', with “the sub-category group overrides the parent group” (single-route). Inference: makes depth affordable by inheriting down the tree.

rows.h: unlimited levels; the Family owns the schema
rows.shape: “an unlimited number of levels (categories, subcategories, subsubcategories..)”; Category.attributes absent — the Family owns the schema. Inference: unlimited levels with no schema on the category is the only safe default when the tree is the customer's.
Merchant-authored product_cat terms — 9 properties, none an attribute set.
Merchant-authored Category tree; ProductType is flat and separate.
Merchant-authored category EAV tree; “0 of 63 Catalog tables join a category to a product attribute” — the attribute set is the schema owner.
